title: An Italian Christmas Eve Feast | Entertainment | thewesterlysun.com
text:
NEW LONDON — Mystic playwright Anna Maria Trusky brings back her 2024 hit, "An Italian Christmas Eve Feast" this weekend and this time to the Oasis Room of the Garde in New London.
Her "festive and original comedy," which she once described as "Neil Simon meets Federico Fellini," is centered upon the members of the Pescatore family, a large Italian-American family headed by Neapolitan immigrants who run a mom-and-pop grocery store.
Guests become part of the Pescatore's Christmas Eve as the begin to celebrate the traditional "Feast of the Seven Fishes."
"An Italian Christmas Eve Feast," said Trusky who not only wrote the play but directs and produced it, calls the show "a hilarious, heartwarming, at-times-zany comedy."
"It's a dinner theater whose main ingredient is love," Trusky explained just before the show's debut, "and the audience gets to be part of the fun."
There are "moments of interaction interspersed throughout the show," she said, noting that the production is an "actual dinner theater experience."
On this Christmas Eve when everyone in the far-flung Pescatore family finally makes it home for the traditional Feast of Seven Fishes. The reunion promises warmth and hilarity — if they can all reconcile a variety of dreams and hopes and differences across time.
Ticketholders will partake in salad, pizza and cannoli prepared by Old Saybrook’s most excellent Luigi’s Wood Fired Pizza Risto.
To complete the spirit of the event and the season, audience members are invited to bring non-perishable food items (or as Rick Koster asked, "Hey, why not dried pasta, jarred sauce, and non-refrigerated grated cheese?"), which will be donated to the United Way’s Gemma Moran Food Bank.
The delightful two-act family comedy takes place in the Garde’s Oasis Room from Dec. 4-7 at 7 p.m. each night at Garde Arts Center, 325 State St., New London. Tickets are $63 at gardearts.org/events/an-italian-christmas-eve-feast or call 860-444-7373, ext. 1.
— Nancy Burns-Fusaro
